answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using proof of space-time. Agents bind their identities to dedicated storage sectors by answering a steady river of challenge queries. This forces an attacker to commit scarce physical drive capacity per identity rather than deploying virtual clones behind a sable facade of software emulators. Consequently, rogue node spikes cannot ripple through task markets. However, operators with mass storage arrays can still centralize control.
